plan:
- Microcontroller (e.g., ESP32 or Arduino Nano), 4-6 micro servo motors, small LiPo battery with charging/boost converter, optional joystick/buttons for control.
- Custom 3D-printed arm segments, base chassis, motor mounts, and an end-effector (e.g., gripper).
- Small ball bearings for joints, various M2/M3 screws and nuts for assembly, adhesive rubber feet for stability.
- Optional: Bluetooth module for wireless control, small breadboard or custom PCB for wiring.

subSteps.title: 3D Print all PLA components
3D Print all PETG components
Prepare the Robot Base Plate
Test fit servos into their mounts
Test fit electrical components into their mounts
Press ball bearings into base housing top
Solder Main Battery to Power Management Module
Wire 5V Power and Ground from Power Management to Main Controller and Servos
Wire 5V Power and Ground from Power Management to Control Joystick
Connect PWM signal wires from Main Controller to all Servos
Connect Analog and Digital signal wires from Main Controller to Control Joystick
Perform continuity checks on all power and signal lines
Connect Main Controller to computer via USB and install drivers
Upload initial firmware to Main Controller with basic servo control code
Verify servo functionality and range of motion for each servo
Test Control Joystick input and read values via serial monitor
Integrate joystick readings into servo control logic in firmware
Calibrate servo endpoints and joystick dead zones for smooth operation
Mount Main Controller, Power Management, and Main Battery into Base Housing Bottom
Attach Base Servo to Base Servo Mount and Fasten to Base Housing Bottom
Assemble Base Housing Top with Control Joystick Mount and Control Joystick
Connect Shoulder Arm Segment to Base Servo and integrate ball bearing
Assemble Shoulder, Elbow, and Wrist Segments with respective servos
Attach Pen Tool Holder/End-Effector with Gripper Servo
Close up the Base Housing and attach to Base Plate
Perform final cable routing, strain relief, and system test

tools: Hot glue gun (optional, for strain relief)
assumptions: Basic understanding of 3D printing and post-processing
Familiarity with soldering small components and wires
Knowledge of microcontroller programming (e.g., Arduino IDE, PlatformIO)
